chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Khayrān al-Asbāṭī, who said:

I came to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام in al-Madīnah, and he said to me: “What is the news of al-Wāthiq with you?” I said: “May I be sacrificed for you, I left him in good health. I am among the people who had most recently seen him; my last meeting with him was ten days ago.” He said: “The people of al-Madīnah are saying that he has died.” So when he said to me, “the people,” I knew that it was he.

Then he said to me: “What happened to Jaʿfar?” I said: “I left him in the worst condition of the people, in prison.” He said: “Indeed, he is the صاحب الأمر. What happened to Ibn al-Zayyāt?” I said: “May I be sacrificed for you, the people are with him, and the authority is his.” He said: “Indeed, it is an ill omen upon him.”

He said: Then he was silent, and said to me: “It is inevitable that the decrees of Allah, the Exalted, and His judgments come to pass. O Khayrān, al-Wāthiq has died, al-Mutawakkil Jaʿfar has taken his seat, and Ibn al-Zayyāt has been killed.” So I said: “When, may I be sacrificed for you?” He said: “Six days after your departure.”

key_terms.أَحْكَامُهُ: His judgments, referring to Allah’s decisive ordinances
key_terms.ابْنُ الزَّيَّاتِ: Ibn al-Zayyāt, the political figure mentioned in the report
key_terms.الْوَاثِقِ: al-Wāthiq, the Abbasid caliph being discussed
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْأَمْرِ: the one who will hold authority or rule
key_terms.مَقَادِيرُ اللَّهِ: the decrees of Allah that inevitably unfold

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the Imam’s knowledge of political events and the unfolding of Allah’s decree?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a report from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام concerning the death of al-Wāthiq, the rise of al-Mutawakkil Jaʿfar, and the killing of Ibn al-Zayyāt. It highlights the unfolding of divine decree and presents the Imam’s knowledge of events before their public confirmation.
